name: CAP (Cyclophosphamide/DOXOrubicin/CISplatin)
cyclesNote: maximum of 8 cycles (DeVita 12th ed., line 77666: given for a maximum of eight 3-week cycles)

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thymomas and Thymic Carcinomas
source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: CAP is a cytotoxic anthracycline/platinum backbone and is not biomarker-restricted. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thymomas and Thymic Carcinomas v2.2026, THYM-C Systemic Therapy Regimens, CAP (cyclophosphamide/doxorubicin/cisplatin) is listed as a first-line regimen for both thymoma and thymic carcinoma.

histology: thymic epithelial tumor (thymoma; also used in thymic carcinoma)

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: CISplatin plus anthracycline is a high-emetic-risk regimen; give per high-emetogenicity antiemetic tier.

supportiveCare: CISplatin: pre and post IV hydration; monitor nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neurotoxicity.
DOXOrubicin: cumulative anthracycline dose tracking and LVEF assessment.
Antiemetics: high emetic risk (cisplatin plus anthracycline). G-CSF per febrile-neutropenia risk assessment (VERIFY against a cited source before asserting a tier).
monitoring: renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each cycle - CISplatin
LVEF and cumulative anthracycline dose tracking - DOXOrubicin
audiometry/neuropathy assessment as clinically indicated - CISplatin

doseModificationRules.condition: declining LVEF or cumulative doxorubicin approaching 450 to 550 mg/m2
doseModificationRules.text: Reassess anthracycline continuation; clinical review required.
Hold or reduce cisplatin and ensure hydration per nephrotoxicity guidance; clinical review.

drugs.name: CISplatin
drugs.route: IV with pre and post hydration
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., lines 77665 to 77666 (Loehrer intergroup CAP for recurrent/metastatic thymoma). CISplatin 50 mg/m2 IV, given day 1 of each 3-week cycle (single-day administration; DeVita states the doses and 3-week cycling, day-of-cycle is the conventional CAP schedule). Requires pre and post IV hydration; monitor nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neurotoxicity. Tall-man per ISMP.

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 77665 to 77666 (Loehrer CAP: cisplatin 50 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2, maximum of eight 3-week cycles, recurrent/metastatic thymoma)

drugs.name: DOXOrubicin
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., lines 77665 to 77666. DOXOrubicin 50 mg/m2 IV, day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Anthracycline: track cumulative lifetime dose (warn 450, hard 550 mg/m2, conventional ceiling, not a dose from the source table); assess LVEF. Tall-man per ISMP.

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., lines 77665 to 77666. Cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2 IV, day 1 of each 3-week cycle.

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
